Subject: Initial capacity ask: expected sustained throughput and network bounds

Grace —

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call earlier. Per our internal planning, we need a concrete sizing baseline for the private GPU pool you will run in our VPC. High-level constraints:

- Target steady-state throughput: ~1200 tokens/sec across 3 model variants (chat-short, chat-long, embeddings-heavy).
- 99th pct latency SLO: 250ms for chat-short (90 token avg), 600ms for chat-long (600 token avg).
- Network: 10G uplink per node; we can request 25G if justified.
- Want guidance on autoscale triggers, warmup time, and how cache-warming affects initial latency.

Can you share a scenario plan (headroom, recommended pool size, and a staging test plan) we can run with our infra team? Attached is our network diagram and a rough traffic trace.

Best,
Alex Park
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask: expected sustained throughput and network bounds

Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask and the diagrams. I sketched three scenarios below (conservative / expected / aggressive) with recommended pool sizes and a short test plan. Attaching a simple capacity_model_v1.xlsx with the math.

Key assumptions:
- Model variants: chat-short (~2.5 tokens/ms raw on A100-80GB equiv), chat-long (lower effective throughput due to longer sequences/kv cache overhead), embeddings-heavy (high CPU preprocessing + modest token output).
- Average concurrency profile: peak 1800 concurrent requests in aggressive case, each chat-short request averages 90 tokens.
- We assume 10G node NIC unless you confirm 25G is available — I'll size both.

Scenarios (summary):
1) Conservative: 12 GPUs (A100-80 equiv), target sustained ~800 tps, headroom ~1.2x, can operate on 10G NICs if we limit ingress concurrency and use request shaping.
2) Expected: 18 GPUs, target ~1,200 tps, warmup-cache strategy required (prefix cache + eager KV fetch), recommend 25G per node or 2x10G LAG.
3) Aggressive: 26 GPUs, target ~2,000 tps, require 25G NICs and additional NIC bonding; need prewarmed replicas and autoscale thresholds tuned to queue depth.

Staging plan (short):
- Week 1: deploy 2-node canary, validate model variants and measure per-token times end-to-end over VPC NAT path.
- Week 2: run incremental soak tests using your trace (10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) while capturing KV hit rates.
- Week 3: run spike test (2x expected) for 15 minutes to validate failover and autoscale.

Next steps: Marcus will drop a sizing calc and Ben will share recommended autoscale triggers and cache-warmup knobs. Can you confirm that 25G is attainable for the expected and aggressive scenarios?

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Adding sizing math and a small worked example to make the choices concrete. Posting the quick table inline — see the spreadsheet for formulas.

Assumptions (worked numbers):
- Chat-short: avg 90 tokens, model latency = 90 tokens / (2.5 tokens/ms) = 36 ms model time; end-to-end (serialization + network + queueing) add ~70 ms => 106 ms per request.
- Effective per-GPU throughput for chat-short (concurrent interleaving): ~9 requests/sec per GPU (conservative); for batching across concurrent streams we see improvement to ~12 req/sec in our lab.

Sizing example (expected scenario):
- Target: 1,200 tokens/sec. If average request emits 90 tokens, that's ~13.3 req/sec needed.
- If each GPU supports 12 req/sec => need ~1.1 GPUs for chat-short alone. But because you have mixed workloads and long chats that hold KV cache and reduce amortized throughput, use a conservative mix factor of 3x => 13 GPUs needed.

Network: 10G NIC per node can sustain ~1.1Gb/s of outbound for our typical token sizes when concurrency is moderate. For the expected pool (18 GPUs) we recommend either 25G or 2x10G LAG to avoid head-of-line blocking during spikes.

Autoscale guidance (short):
- Primary trigger: queue depth hitting 50 concurrent pending requests above target for >30s.
- Secondary trigger: CPU or VRAM pressure on the replica > 85% for >20s.
- Cooldown: 3m after scale-up; 10m before scale-down to avoid flapping.

I'll attach a small sensitivity table in the spreadsheet (tokens per req variance +- 25%).

— Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick notes on warmup/caching impact and rollout strategy:

- Cold start penalty: in our tests, a fully cold model (empty KV cache) shows 2–3x latency on the first request for a prefix-heavy workload. That matters for canaries and sudden routing changes.
- Warmup plan: pre-initialize KV caches using representative prompts (we recommend a short set of 200 warmup prompts per model variant) and keep a small always-on prewarmed pool (1–2 GPUs).
- Cache eviction: set TTLs per model class — chat-long TTL longer than chat-short. We can also instrument cache-hit heatmaps to tune.

Rollout suggestion: canary with 2% traffic, ramp to 25% over 1 hour if tail latencies remain within thresholds; use automated rollback on 95th pct latency regression > 20% or error rate > 0.5%.

Ben Carter
Ops Reliability — Redwood Inference
